questionText: A circular coil of $100$ turns and area of cross-section $10^{-2}\text{ m}^2$ is rotated about its vertical diameter at $60\text{ rpm}$ in a uniform horizontal magnetic field of $3.5 \times 10^{-2}\text{ T}$. The maximum emf induced in the coil is:
detailedSolution:

Given:

- Area of cross-section: $A = 10^{-2}\text{ m}^2$
- Rotation frequency: $\nu = 60\text{ rpm} = \frac{60}{60}\text{ rev/s} = 1\text{ rev/s}$
- Angular velocity: $\omega = 2\pi\nu = 2\pi(1) = 2\pi\text{ rad/s}$
- Magnetic field: $B = 3.5 \times 10^{-2}\text{ T}$

The peak induced EMF is:
$$\mathcal{E}_0 = N B A \omega$$
Substitute the values:
$$\mathcal{E}_0 = 100 \times (3.5 \times 10^{-2}\text{ T}) \times (10^{-2}\text{ m}^2) \times (2\pi\text{ rad/s})$$
$$\mathcal{E}_0 = 3.5 \times 10^{-2} \times 2\pi = 7\pi \times 10^{-2}\text{ V}$$
Using $\pi \approx 3.1416$:
$$\mathcal{E}_0 = 0.07 \times 3.1416 = 0.2199\text{ V} \approx 0.22\text{ V}$$
Option C is correct.

Therefore, option (C) is the correct answer.
